screening_decisions.reason: Descriptive survey study using focus groups and questionnaires; not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial.
Program evaluation with before-after comparison; no randomisation or quasi-randomisation described.
Randomised trial but facility-based (health facilities randomized); intervention delivered in antenatal clinics, not community-based.
Systematic review of existing studies; not a primary trial.
Randomised controlled trial but outcomes focus on infant care practices and family planning, not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity.
Review article summarizing evidence; not a primary trial.
Randomised controlled trial of community postnatal support but outcomes are depression and general health, not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity.
Cluster randomised controlled trial of community-based women's groups intervention with neonatal mortality as primary outcome; meets all criteria.
Pilot cluster randomised trial of community-based Lady Health Workers delivering door-to-door health promotion; addresses maternal and neonatal health practices.
Quasi-experimental design with intervention and control areas evaluating antenatal and postnatal care measures for maternal mortality reduction.
Randomised controlled trial but outcomes focus on child development and parenting, not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity.
Protocol paper describing planned trial; no results reported.
Process evaluation within a cluster-randomised controlled trial of community-based maternal-neonatal health package; addresses neonatal illness surveillance and referral.
Community-based antenatal education evaluation but does not describe randomisation; appears to be non-randomized comparison.
Quasi-experimental design evaluating skilled care initiative on pregnancy-related mortality in rural Burkina Faso; meets criteria.
Community-based randomised controlled trial evaluating prenatal care intervention and perinatal outcomes; meets all criteria.
Commentary/opinion piece on community participation; not a trial.
Cluster randomised controlled trial of community mobilization (women's groups) targeting perinatal care and outcomes including stillbirths and neonatal deaths.
Cluster randomised trial of community postnatal care but outcomes are mental health/depression, not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity.
Quasi-experimental design evaluating community-based integrated nutrition and health programme with neonatal mortality as primary outcome; meets all criteria.

This is a randomised stepped-wedge trial evaluating a community-based intervention package (clean delivery kits plus education on 'six cleans') that addresses maternal and neonatal morbidity (cord infection and puerperal sepsis). Meets all selection criteria.

This is a qualitative study using in-depth interviews to identify barriers to maternal healthcare. It is not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

While this is a community-based RCT, the primary outcome is infant immunization completion rates, not maternal or neonatal mortality/morbidity. The intervention focuses on vaccine education rather than a comprehensive community-based intervention package for maternal/neonatal health outcomes.
This is a systematic analysis providing estimates of child mortality causes globally. It is not a primary trial evaluating an intervention. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is a cluster-randomised trial but the outcomes are maternal depression and physical health scores, not maternal or neonatal mortality/morbidity. The intervention does not target the specified outcomes in the selection criteria.

This is described as a 'controlled study' comparing communities with different levels of TBA access. While it mentions 'randomly selected' communities, the study design does not appear to be a randomised or quasi-randomised trial with intervention allocation. The comparison is observational based on existing access patterns.
This is a systematic review of existing studies on severe acute maternal morbidity. It is not a primary trial evaluating an intervention. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a commentary/opinion paper discussing maternal health in broader context. It is not a trial evaluating an intervention. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is a field trial with intervention and control villages evaluating a community-based intervention package (home-based neonatal care including sepsis management, health education, trained birth attendants). The study reports significant reductions in neonatal, infant, and perinatal mortality. While randomisation is not explicitly stated, the quasi-experimental design with intervention and control areas fits the quasi-randomised trial criteria.

This is a randomised trial but the outcomes are depressive symptoms, stress, and psychosocial resources, not maternal or neonatal mortality/morbidity. The intervention does not target the specified outcomes in the selection criteria.
This is a review article discussing maternal mortality patterns and causes. It is not a trial evaluating an intervention. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is an observational study using demographic surveillance data. The authors explicitly state 'Caution is required in the interpretation of short-term trends in one indicator in studies designed without random allocation of interventions into treatment and control groups.' Does not meet study design criteria.

This is a quasi-experimental study with one intervention district and one comparison district evaluating a community-based maternal and neonatal health programme. The study measures programme coverage, maternal and newborn care practices, and health care utilization. Quasi-randomised trials are included in the selection criteria.

This is an RCT but the intervention is a single component (chimney stove to reduce wood smoke exposure) rather than a comprehensive community-based intervention package. The outcome is birth weight only, not maternal/neonatal mortality or broader morbidity outcomes.
This is a methodology chapter about statistical methods for meta-analysis. It is not a trial evaluating an intervention. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of seven RCTs. While it reviews relevant trials, it is not itself a primary trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is a pilot study with cluster design (four intervention vs four comparison village clusters) evaluating a community-based intervention package (LHWs, traditional birth attendants, community health committees). The study reports significant reductions in stillbirth and neonatal mortality. While described as a pilot requiring confirmation, it presents results from a community-based intervention package targeting the specified outcomes.

This is an RCT but the outcomes are behavioral risk factors (cigarette smoking, depression, intimate partner violence) rather than maternal or neonatal mortality/morbidity. The intervention is clinic-based counseling, not a community-based intervention package.

This appears to be a protocol or study description paper outlining the design of a planned cluster-randomised trial. The abstract describes what the study 'aims to test' and 'will be conducted' rather than reporting completed results. Without reported outcomes, it cannot be evaluated against the selection criteria.

This is a cluster-randomised effectiveness trial evaluating a community-based intervention package (antenatal care promotion, maternal health education, clean delivery kits, facility births, immediate newborn care, danger sign identification, care-seeking promotion) delivered through LHWs, traditional birth attendants, and community health committees. Primary outcomes are perinatal and neonatal mortality. Meets all selection criteria.
Economic evaluation alongside a trial, not the primary effectiveness trial.
Cross-sectional survey, not a randomized trial.
Review article, not a primary trial.
High-income setting (US), outcomes focus on hospitalization/repeat pregnancy rather than mortality/morbidity in LMIC context.
High-income setting (UK), outcomes focus on mental/physical health scores rather than mortality.
High-income setting (US), outcomes are service utilization, not mortality/morbidity.
Cluster-RCT, community-based intervention package, LMIC setting, evaluates neonatal mortality.
High-income setting (UK), outcomes do not include mortality.
Prospective cohort study, not a randomized trial.
Opinion/Commentary article, not a primary trial.
Policy document/report, not a primary trial.
Diagnostic accuracy/validation study, not an effectiveness trial.
Contains a cluster-RCT component evaluating community-based training on neonatal/perinatal mortality in developing countries.
Cluster-RCT, community-based intervention package, LMIC setting, evaluates perinatal and maternal mortality.
Quasi-experimental design evaluating community mobilization on mortality in LMIC. Included conservatively due to relevance and lack of strict randomization.
Pre-post design without concurrent control/randomization, does not meet trial criteria.
Secondary analysis focusing on retention, not primary effectiveness evaluation.
Sub-study/process evaluation of a larger trial, focuses on referral compliance not mortality.
Non-randomized pre-post study, not a trial.
Cluster-RCT, community-based intervention package, LMIC setting, evaluates neonatal mortality and care behaviors.

This is a before-after observational study comparing villages that joined a PHC programme with those that did not (based on village size). It is not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial as required by the selection criteria.

While this is an RCT, the intervention is facility-based antenatal health education (not a community-based intervention package), and the outcomes are maternal health behaviors (post-partum visit attendance, birth preparedness) rather than maternal/neonatal mortality, morbidity, or neonatal outcomes.
This is a descriptive study analyzing trends using CHW records, hospital registers, and household surveys. It is not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial.
This appears to be a Cochrane review protocol/abstract only, not a primary trial. The abstract is incomplete and does not describe a specific trial evaluating a community-based intervention package.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled trials, not a primary randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial.

This is a study protocol presenting baseline characteristics for a cluster-RCT. While the intervention (CHW home visits) is community-based, this is a protocol paper without results, and the selection criteria requires trials \'evaluating the effectiveness\' - protocols do not report effectiveness outcomes.

While this is an RCT, the intervention is a nursing education program (not a community-based intervention package), the sample is very small (n=20), and the outcomes are maternal role attainment and maternal-fetal attachment rather than maternal/neonatal mortality, morbidity, or neonatal outcomes.
This is an observational study comparing neonates who received CHW home visits with those who did not. It is not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial.
This is a before-after study using two household surveys (baseline 2002 and endline 2004). It is not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial.

This is a study protocol for a cluster-RCT. While it describes a community-based intervention package targeting neonatal mortality, it is a protocol without results, and the selection criteria requires trials \'evaluating the effectiveness\' - protocols do not report effectiveness outcomes.

While this is an RCT with a community-based intervention (home visits by lay community workers), the outcomes are mother-infant relationship quality, infant attachment security, and maternal depression - not maternal/neonatal mortality, morbidity, or neonatal outcomes as required by the selection criteria.

This is a factorial cluster-randomised controlled trial evaluating community-based intervention packages (women\'s groups and volunteer peer counsellor home visits). The outcomes include maternal mortality rate, neonatal mortality rate, infant mortality rate, and breastfeeding rates - all matching the selection criteria.

This is a pilot study with a matched comparison group, not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. Additionally, the outcomes (maternal mood, mother-infant relationship, infant growth) do not match the required maternal/neonatal mortality, morbidity, or neonatal outcomes.

This is a cluster-randomised controlled trial evaluating a community-based intervention package (home visits by community-based surveillance volunteers promoting essential newborn care practices). The primary outcome is neonatal mortality rate, with secondary outcomes including newborn care practices - matching the selection criteria.

This is a cluster-randomised controlled trial evaluating a community-based intervention package (participatory women\'s groups addressing maternal and newborn health problems). The primary outcomes include neonatal mortality rate and maternal depression scores - matching the selection criteria.

This is a secondary analysis of data from a cluster-randomised trial evaluating training of birth attendants (WHO Essential Newborn Care program and neonatal resuscitation program) - a community-based intervention. The outcomes are perinatal mortality and early neonatal mortality, matching the selection criteria.

While this is an RCT, the intervention is social support (non-directive listening visits) in a developed country setting (London), and the outcomes are maternal depression, child injury, and maternal smoking - not maternal/neonatal mortality, morbidity, or neonatal outcomes as required.

This is an observational study (secondary analysis of RESPIRE trial data) examining associations between CO exposure and neurodevelopmental performance in school-age children. The outcomes are not maternal/neonatal mortality, morbidity, or neonatal outcomes, and it is not evaluating a community-based intervention package for maternal/neonatal health.

While this is a cluster-randomised trial, the intervention is a health system financing mechanism (payment for performance) targeting health facilities, not a community-based intervention package. The outcomes are service utilization (prenatal care visits, institutional deliveries, immunisation) rather than maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity.

While this is a cluster-randomised trial, the intervention is birth plans developed during antenatal care (facility-based), and the outcomes are skilled delivery care uptake and postnatal care utilisation - service utilization outcomes rather than maternal/neonatal mortality, morbidity, or neonatal outcomes.

RCT with community postnatal support workers, but primary outcomes are cost-effectiveness and general health status (SF-36), not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity. Does not meet outcome criteria.

Reports baseline prevalence data from a cluster-randomized trial, not an evaluation of intervention effectiveness. This is a cross-sectional analysis of depressed mood prevalence, not an RCT evaluating community-based intervention packages.
Cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluating facilitation of local stakeholder groups (community-based intervention) with neonatal mortality as primary outcome. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized clinical trial but explicitly clinic-based intervention ('clinic-based, individually tailored counseling sessions'), not community-based. Does not meet community-based criterion.
Randomized controlled trial with community-based peer counsellors conducting home visits. Primary outcome is exclusive breastfeeding, which is a neonatal outcome. Meets all selection criteria.
Prospective community-based cluster randomized controlled trial evaluating WHO Essential Newborn Care training. Primary outcome is perinatal mortality. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial of community-based postnatal home visits. Outcomes include maternal postpartum morbidities, infant morbidity, and neonatal health practices. Meets all selection criteria.

Community randomized controlled effectiveness trial promoting exclusive breastfeeding and complementary feeding practices. Outcomes include breastfeeding, nutritional intake, and supplementation coverage. Meets all selection criteria.
Study compares midwives vs paraprofessionals but does not describe randomization. Appears to be an observational comparison rather than a randomized trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

Quasi-experimental evaluation of community-based breastfeeding promotion programme. Quasi-randomised designs are acceptable per selection criteria. Focuses on breastfeeding prevalence, a neonatal outcome.
Cluster randomized controlled trial of community-based exclusive breastfeeding promotion. Outcomes include exclusive breastfeeding, diarrhoeal illness, and growth. Meets all selection criteria.
Review article summarizing 15 TBA- and midwife-based interventions, not a primary randomized trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

Randomized controlled trial of postnatal social support, but primary outcomes are child injury, maternal smoking, and maternal depression - not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity. Does not meet outcome criteria.
Randomized trial of community-based health education with home visits. Outcomes include perinatal mortality, prematurity, and breastfeeding practices. Meets all selection criteria.
Longitudinal study with intervention and comparison area, but no randomization described. Does not meet study design criteria for RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-randomised trial.
Prospective cluster randomized controlled study of traditional birth attendant training. Primary outcome is neonatal mortality. Meets all selection criteria.
Cluster-randomized controlled trial of community-based CBT intervention for maternal depression. Outcomes include maternal depression and infant weight/height. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized community intervention trial comparing antenatal care packages. Outcomes include preventable neonatal morbidity, low birth weight, and maternal morbidity. Meets all selection criteria.
Observational study comparing two districts using household census and logistic regression. No randomization described. Does not meet study design criteria.

Randomized controlled trial of automated H1N1 symptom monitoring. While community-based, the focus is on influenza detection/treatment, not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity. Does not meet outcome criteria.

Community-based health promotion programme carried out by local women targeting neonatal tetanus mortality. While randomization is not explicitly stated, there is comparison between intervention and control areas. As a conservative approach, including this study that evaluates a community-based intervention package affecting neonatal mortality.

Cluster randomized controlled trial evaluating community-based participatory intervention with women's groups. Primary outcomes include neonatal mortality rate and maternal mortality ratio. Clearly meets all selection criteria: RCT design, community-based intervention package, maternal and neonatal outcomes.

Intervention implemented in pilot zone compared with control area. Includes community health education and safe motherhood interventions. While randomization is not explicitly described, the study compares intervention vs control areas for maternal mortality outcomes. Including conservatively due to uncertainty about study design.

Randomized controlled trial but focuses specifically on adolescent mothers (special population subset). While it includes community-based home visitation, the primary focus is on social outcomes (school dropout) and infant morbidity rather than maternal/neonatal mortality. The population restriction makes it less relevant to the broader review question.

This is a systematic review/article reviewing evidence, not a primary trial. Selection criteria require prospective randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trials. Reviews do not meet the study design criteria.

Secondary analysis of an RCT focusing on perinatal depression as the primary outcome. The review protocol specifies maternal and neonatal mortality/morbidity and neonatal outcomes. Depression is a maternal mental health outcome, not directly related to mortality or morbidity as defined in the protocol.

This is a commentary/series article discussing cost-effectiveness of interventions, not a primary trial. No actual trial data presented. Does not meet the study design criteria requiring randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trials.

While this includes a randomized controlled study component with community-based elements, the primary outcomes are knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors rather than maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity. The review protocol specifically requires outcomes related to mortality and morbidity reduction.

Two-by-two factorial cluster randomized controlled trial evaluating community intervention (women's groups) combined with facility-based quality improvement. Primary outcomes include maternal, perinatal, and neonatal mortality. Clearly meets all selection criteria.

Community-based peer-counseling intervention with comparison to control area. Exclusive breastfeeding is a key neonatal health outcome. While randomization is not explicitly stated, the study compares intervention vs control areas. Including conservatively as breastfeeding is a recognized neonatal health outcome.

This is a 7-year follow-up study of an original RCT, assessing outcomes at age 8 years. The outcomes measured (parenting skills, library visits, homework checking, immunization completion) are not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity. The time frame and outcomes fall outside the review scope.

Community-based intervention strengthening women's organizations with perinatal mortality as primary outcome. While the design appears to be before-after rather than randomized, it evaluates a community-based intervention package affecting perinatal mortality. Including conservatively due to uncertainty about whether this might qualify as quasi-randomized.

Cluster randomized controlled trial evaluating IMNCI programme which includes community health worker home visits and women's group meetings. Primary outcomes include neonatal and infant mortality. Clearly meets all selection criteria for community-based intervention package with appropriate outcomes.

Cluster-randomized trial evaluating community-based intervention (TBA training) with perinatal mortality mentioned as outcome. The intervention is delivered at community level through trained TBAs. Meets criteria for cluster-randomized trial with community-based intervention affecting maternal/neonatal outcomes.

Cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluating community-based behavior change intervention package for essential newborn care. Primary outcome is neonatal mortality rate. Delivered by community health workers via collective meetings and household visits. Clearly meets all selection criteria.
